newsitem.title: UK: Airtours summer bookings jump 57 pct.
newsitem.headline: Airtours summer bookings jump 57 pct.

text.p: British package holiday company Airtours Plc said on Wednesday that key summer bookings were 57.2 percent ahead of last year, although the figure would fall as the tour operator sells out of stock.

Airtours, which sells tours to holiday makers in Britain, Scandinavia and Canada, beat expectations by posting a sharp 46 percent rise in annual pre-tax profits to 86.8 million pounds ($143.5 million) and raised its total dividend to 16p from 12.75p.

"These results show that the group is in excellent condition and we look forward to the future with confidence," said chairman and chief executive David Crossland. "The outlook for 1996/97 in all of our major markets is encouraging."
Record profits were helped by "excellent results" from the company's Scandinavian businesses and careful pricing in Britain in an industry where capacity had fallen, Airtours said.

The company, which says it is now the largest air-inclusive tour operator in the world, said it would keep capacity at around summer 1996 levels. If this position were maintained across the industry, the "rewards could be substantial".

In Scandinavia, winter bookings were 92 percent ahead of last year, while the more important summer season was not yet on sale. But Airtours said trading conditions in Canada remained difficult and further rationalisation was likely in the highly fragmented market.
Winter bookings, the main holiday season in Canada, were 58.9 percent ahead of last year. ($1=.6047 Pound)
